_meta.purpose: Canonical hyperscaler systems + cloud architecture invariants for product PRD hyperscaler_bar evidence. This is the source of truth for hyperscaler-grade architecture requirements; product-level blocking remains advisory until the PRD validator and branch-protected lane land.
_meta.user_directive_2026_05_17: Take hyperscaler systems architecture and cloud architecture in mind as well

invariants.rule: No service shares mutable state across cells. A cell is an independent failure domain bounded by region + AZ + shard. Cross-cell traffic is blocked by default via network ACL and Cedar policy deny.
invariants.rationale: Eliminates US-East-1-class blast radius. Source: AWS Builders Library — 'Workload isolation using shuffle-sharding' (https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/workload-isolation-using-shuffle-sharding/). Also per ADR-0033 cell-domain crates and ADR-0114 canary cohort-per-cell model.

invariants.rule: Tenant-to-cell assignment uses shuffle-sharding (not simple modulo). Each tenant maps to a small random subset of cells so a noisy tenant's blast radius cannot exceed its assigned subset.
invariants.rationale: AWS Builders Library — 'Workload isolation using shuffle-sharding' (https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/workload-isolation-using-shuffle-sharding/). Simple modulo hashing means a noisy tenant can impact 1/N of all tenants; shuffle-sharding bounds impact to subset size.

invariants.rule: Every service continues to operate using cached/local state when its control plane or dependency is degraded. No service hard-fails on control-plane unavailability during steady-state operations.
invariants.rationale: AWS Builders Library — 'Static stability using Availability Zones' (https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/static-stability-using-availability-zones/). Services that depend on a control plane for runtime decisions fail catastrophically when that plane is unavailable.

invariants.rule: Every mutating API operation accepts an idempotency key. Replaying the same key with identical payload returns the same result and produces no duplicate side-effects.
invariants.rationale: Stripe Engineering — 'Idempotent requests' (https://stripe.com/docs/api/idempotent_requests). Distributed systems retry on timeout; without idempotency, retries create duplicate charges, records, or state transitions. Palantir Foundry uses operation tokens for the same guarantee.

invariants.rule: Every service that emits events to a message bus does so via a transactional outbox: the event row is written atomically with the state change in the same DB transaction, then a relay process publishes it.
invariants.rationale: Microsoft Azure Architecture Center — 'Outbox pattern' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/best-practices/transactional-outbox-cosmos). Dual-write (DB + broker in one transaction) is impossible in distributed systems; the outbox is the only correct pattern for at-least-once delivery with no phantom events.

invariants.rule: Every multi-step distributed transaction is implemented as a saga with explicit compensation steps. No distributed two-phase commit (2PC) is permitted across service boundaries.
invariants.rationale: Microsoft Azure Architecture Center — 'Saga distributed transactions pattern' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/reference-architectures/saga/saga). 2PC across services creates blocking locks and cascading failures; saga with compensation achieves eventual consistency without cross-service locking.

invariants.rule: Every synchronous cross-service call is wrapped in a circuit breaker (open on threshold; half-open probe; closed on recovery). Thread/connection pools are bulkheaded per downstream so a slow dependency cannot exhaust shared resources.
invariants.rationale: Netflix Tech Blog — 'Hystrix circuit breaker' (https://netflixtechblog.com/fault-tolerance-in-a-high-volume-distributed-system-91ab4faae74a). Google SRE Book Chapter 22 — 'Addressing Cascading Failures'. Without circuit breakers, a slow dependency cascades latency to all callers.

invariants.rule: Every service enforces backpressure at its ingress. When queue depth or latency exceeds threshold, the service sheds load via 503 with Retry-After rather than accepting unbounded work and degrading for all callers.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Workbook — 'Eliminating Toil' (https://sre.google/workbook/eliminating-toil/) and Chapter 21 'Handling Overload'. AWS Builders Library — 'Using load shedding to avoid overload' (https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/). Accepting unbounded work amplifies latency non-linearly per Little's Law.

invariants.rule: No service implements a silent fallback path that serves stale or degraded data without surfacing a signal to the caller. Degraded responses MUST include an explicit degraded indicator in the response envelope.
invariants.rationale: AWS Builders Library — 'Avoiding fallback in distributed systems' (https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/avoiding-fallback-in-distributed-systems/). Silent fallbacks hide failures, cause silent data divergence, and make incidents harder to detect and bound.

invariants.rule: Every production-tier service has a documented and drill-verified multi-region failover path. RTO ≤ 30 min, RPO ≤ 5 min for Tier-1 services. Failover drills run quarterly and produce evidence.
invariants.rationale: AWS Well-Architected Framework — Reliability Pillar (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/reliability-pillar/welcome.html). Google SRE Book — 'Handling Overload' + availability table (https://sre.google/sre-book/availability-table/). RTO/RPO targets directly map to SLO availability commitments.

invariants.rule: Every cell reserves capacity headroom of ≥ 30% above peak-measured load. Capacity is validated against actual traffic profiles, not theoretical estimates. Capacity reviews run monthly.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Book — 'Being On-Call' + Chapter 17 'Testing for Reliability' capacity planning sections (https://sre.google/sre-book/being-on-call/). AWS Well-Architected Reliability Pillar: 'Manage service quotas and constraints'. Insufficient headroom means the first spike triggers a cascade.

invariants.rule: Every Tier-1 and Tier-2 service defines SLOs with numeric targets and an error budget policy. The error budget policy defines: budget healthy → ship; budget at 50% → caution; budget exhausted → feature freeze + stabilization sprint.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Workbook — 'Error Budget Policy' (https://sre.google/workbook/error-budget-policy/). SLO-driven release gates are the single most effective mechanism for aligning reliability and velocity incentives.

invariants.rule: Every production service exposes all four golden signals: latency (p50/p95/p99), traffic (RPS), errors (4xx/5xx rate), saturation (CPU/memory/queue depth). Dashboards and burn-rate alerts are required before a service enters production.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Book — 'Monitoring Distributed Systems' (https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/). The four golden signals are the minimum viable observability surface for diagnosing production incidents.

invariants.rule: Every infrastructure resource (CPU, memory, disk, network, queue) is instrumented for the USE method: Utilization, Saturation, Errors. Saturation alerts fire before utilization exceeds 70% of capacity.
invariants.rationale: Brendan Gregg — 'The USE Method' (https://www.brendangregg.com/usemethod.html). The USE method closes the gap between high-level SLO signals and low-level resource exhaustion, enabling pre-incident capacity response.

invariants.rule: Every service propagates W3C trace context (traceparent/tracestate) on all inbound and outbound calls. Every request that crosses a service boundary emits a span with service name, operation, status, and duration. Sampling rate ≥ 1% in production; 100% for error traces.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Workbook — Chapter 4 'Monitoring' distributed tracing section. OpenTelemetry specification (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/traces/). Without end-to-end tracing, production incidents in multi-service paths require hours of log correlation.

invariants.rule: Every service emits structured JSON logs. Every log line includes: timestamp (RFC 3339), service, trace_id, span_id, level, message. No unstructured or printf-style log lines in production code paths.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Book — 'Monitoring Distributed Systems'. AWS Well-Architected Operational Excellence Pillar: 'Implement observability'. Structured logs are machine-parseable and enable SLO burn-rate alerts, audit queries, and incident correlation at scale.

invariants.rule: Every Sev-1 and Sev-2 incident produces a blameless postmortem within 5 business days. The postmortem includes: timeline, root cause, contributing factors, action items with owners and due dates, and at least one mechanical prevention.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Book — 'Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure' (https://sre.google/sre-book/postmortem-culture/). Blameless postmortems are the primary mechanism for converting incidents into systemic improvements. 'You can't fix people, only their environment.'

invariants.rule: Every service identity holds only the IAM permissions required for its current operational tasks. Wildcard resource ARNs and Action:* grants are forbidden. Permissions are reviewed and rotated quarterly.
invariants.rationale: AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar — 'Grant least privilege' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/welcome.html). NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture. Over-permissioned identities are the primary attack vector in cloud breaches.

invariants.rule: Every data store holding Tier-2 or higher data uses envelope encryption: a data encryption key (DEK) encrypts the data; a key encryption key (KEK) stored in KMS/OpenBao encrypts the DEK. Key rotation is automated and occurs ≥ annually.
invariants.rationale: AWS Key Management Service best practices (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/best-practices.html). Google Cloud — 'Envelope encryption' (https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/envelope-encryption). Envelope encryption allows key rotation without re-encrypting the entire dataset.

invariants.rule: Every service enforces a data perimeter: data classified above a tenant's allowed residency boundary cannot leave that boundary via any API, replication, or log path. Audit-chain is emitted on every cross-boundary data ship.
invariants.rationale: AWS — 'Establishing a data perimeter on AWS' (https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/establishing-a-data-perimeter-on-aws/). Data residency violations are a regulatory blocker in KR/JP/EU markets. Per cloud PRD §10 risk: 'Cross-region replication leaks under residency-strict policy'.

invariants.rule: Every build artifact is produced at SLSA Level 2 or higher: hermetic build, provenance attestation (Sigstore/Cosign keyless), and SBOM emission (Syft CycloneDX). Unsigned artifacts are rejected at the admission gate.
invariants.rationale: SLSA Framework (https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/). Cosign keyless signing (https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/signing/signing_with_containers/). AWS re:Invent 2023 — supply chain attacks now target build pipelines, not just runtime. Per ADR-0039 and hyperscaler-best-practices.md §top-3-gaps item A.

invariants.rule: Workloads handling Tier-3 or higher data (PII, health records, financial secrets) run inside a confidential computing boundary (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, or AWS Nitro Enclaves). Attestation of the enclave is verified before secrets are provisioned.
invariants.rationale: AWS Nitro Enclaves — 'Isolated compute for sensitive data' (https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/nitro/nitro-enclaves/). Google Confidential VMs (https://cloud.google.com/confidential-computing). Per cloud PRD §10 risk: 'KVM / hypervisor escape' — confidential compute is the defense-in-depth layer when the hypervisor boundary is insufficient.

invariants.rule: Every cross-axis contract invocation, IAM mutation, data-class promotion, and policy override emits an immutable audit-chain record. Audit records are append-only, signed, and retained for ≥ 7 years for Tier-2+ data.
invariants.rationale: SOC 2 Type II CC7.2 audit logging requirements. KISA K-ISMS-P audit log controls. Per oyatie doctrine: 'audit-chain emission on cross-axis flow' is already identified as a hyperscaler-bar differentiator in hyperscaler-best-practices.md §executive-summary.

invariants.rule: Every production deployment uses progressive delivery: canary cohort → staged rollout → full rollout. Automated rollback fires when SLO burn-rate exceeds 3× in any 5-minute window during rollout.
invariants.rationale: Per ADR-0114 canary observability gate. Argo Rollouts progressive delivery (ADR-0050). Google SRE Workbook — 'Progressive Delivery' (https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/). hyperscaler-best-practices.md §top-3-gaps item B: 'progressive-delivery rails are absent from RELEASE-MANAGEMENT.md'.

invariants.rule: When an upstream provider (cloud API, external SaaS, DNS) enters a degraded state, the consuming service sheds non-critical load, activates cached fallback only with explicit degraded signal, and emits a structured degradation event within 30 seconds.
invariants.rationale: AWS Builders Library — 'Avoiding fallback in distributed systems'. Google SRE Book Chapter 22 'Addressing Cascading Failures'. Per ADR-0114: Foundry canary gate verdict ROLLBACK must fire within a bounded window.

invariants.rule: Every repeatable operational task that runs more than twice per sprint must be automated. Toil ratio (manual ops time / total eng time) is measured per team per quarter and must stay below 20%.
invariants.rationale: Google SRE Workbook — 'Eliminating Toil' (https://sre.google/workbook/eliminating-toil/). 'Anything mechanical must be scripted; never manually iterate deterministic work' per oyatie autonomous-decision-principles feedback.

invariants.rule: Every cloud resource is tagged with: product, team, env (dev/staging/production), cell, and cost-center. Untagged resources are rejected at provisioning time. Unit economics (cost per request / cost per tenant) are computed and reviewed monthly.
invariants.rationale: AWS Well-Architected Cost Optimization Pillar — 'Practice cloud financial management' (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/cost-optimization-pillar/welcome.html). Per cloud PRD §10 risk: 'FinOps unit economics red at GA' — untagged resources make cost attribution impossible at scale.

invariants.rule: Every product reports carbon intensity (gCO2eq per request) and energy efficiency (useful work per watt). Sustainability targets are set annually and reviewed against AWS/Google sustainability benchmarks. Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) ≤ 1.4 for owned infrastructure.
invariants.rationale: AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/sustainability-pillar/welcome.html). Google — 'Operating at 90% carbon-free energy' (https://sustainability.google/progress/energy/). Sustainability is now a procurement gate at enterprise customers.

invariants.rule: Every tenant's data is stored and processed only in the regions permitted by their data residency policy. Cross-region replication requires explicit policy allow + audit-chain event. Air-gapped sovereign cells never egress to non-sovereign networks.
invariants.rationale: GDPR Article 46 (cross-border transfers). Korea PIPA Chapter 6 (cross-border transfers). Per cloud PRD §10 risk: 'Cross-region replication leaks under residency-strict policy'. Per ADR-0050 air-gap-first profile for sovereign cells.

invariants.rule: No tenant can read, write, or infer the existence of another tenant's data through any API, timing side-channel, or shared resource. Tenant isolation is enforced at the Cedar policy layer, network ACL layer, and storage encryption layer independently.
invariants.rationale: AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar — 'Protecting data in transit and at rest'. Palantir Foundry — tenant namespace isolation (https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/security/). Defense-in-depth across three independent layers ensures no single bypass creates cross-tenant leakage.

invariants.rule: All static assets, API responses cacheable for ≥ 60 seconds, and public read-only content are served via CDN edge PoPs. Cache-hit rate ≥ 80% for eligible endpoints. Origin traffic for cacheable content ≤ 20% of total.
invariants.rationale: AWS Well-Architected Performance Efficiency Pillar — 'Use caching'. Cloudflare — 'CDN performance benchmarks 2025'. Serving uncacheable content from origin at hyperscaler scale is a cost and latency anti-pattern.

invariants.rule: Every cross-service contract is defined in a machine-readable schema (Protobuf or JSON Schema) with strict typing. Runtime deserialization failures are treated as Sev-2 incidents. No stringly-typed cross-service payloads.
invariants.rationale: Stripe Engineering — 'API design at Stripe' (https://stripe.com/blog/payment-api-design). Linear — 'Type-safe APIs with Rust and GraphQL' (https://linear.app/blog). Palantir Conjure type-safe RPC (https://github.com/palantir/conjure). Stringly-typed payloads degrade silently; schema-enforced contracts fail loudly at the boundary.

invariants.rule: Every data transformation (ETL, aggregation, ML feature derivation) records its lineage: source dataset + schema version, transform applied, output dataset + schema version, and run timestamp. Lineage graph is queryable within 5 minutes of any transform completing.
invariants.rationale: Palantir Foundry — 'Data Lineage' (https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/transforms-overview/). Apache Atlas lineage model. Regulators (GDPR Art. 30, KISA K-ISMS-P) require demonstrable data lineage for audit. Without it, compliance evidence production takes days.

invariants.rule: Every user-facing API endpoint has a defined p99 latency SLO. Homepage/critical-path endpoints: p99 ≤ 200 ms at 10k RPS. Background jobs do not block API paths. CI pipeline p99 ≤ 5 min end-to-end.
invariants.rationale: Linear — 'Why we're obsessed with performance' (https://linear.app/blog/why-were-obsessed-with-performance). Google — 'The impact of web performance' (https://web.dev/performance/). Stripe — latency budgets per API endpoint. Speed is not a feature to optimize later; it is a first-class product requirement from day one.

invariants.rule: Every Rust dependency is audited via cargo-vet alongside cargo-deny and cargo-audit. The vet audit trail records the reviewer, rationale, and criteria met for every dependency in the transitive closure. Unvetted dependencies are blocked at CI.
invariants.rationale: Mozilla Security Engineering — 'cargo-vet: supply chain security for Rust' (https://mozilla.github.io/cargo-vet/). AWS uses cargo-vet for Rust Lambda and Firecracker dependency auditing. Per hyperscaler-best-practices.md §top-3-gaps item C: 'cargo-vet supply-chain audit trail is absent'.
